facts.statement: Born Mhow 1862, died 1936; commissioned 1882, transferred to Indian Army 1884.
Received Victoria Cross for actions during the Ashanti War of 1900.
Commanded in Mesopotamia and endured captivity after Kut; tried to assist other prisoners.
KCMG granted following repatriation at the end of 1918; the NAM account does not establish the precise award date. Retired 1920.

en.tagline: The hunter, the decorated officer and the prisoners of Kut.
en.intro: Melliss’s early book belongs to the dangerous pursuit of big game. His later papers tell a different story of danger: command in Mesopotamia, the surrender at Kut and efforts to keep fellow prisoners alive.
en.orientation: The sporting author and the senior officer must be kept in chronological proportion. Lion-Hunting in Somali-land appeared in 1895, before the Victoria Cross and the commands of the First World War.
origin: Born at Mhow into a military family, he received a commission in 1882 and transferred to the Indian Army in 1884.
career: African and Indian service included the Ashanti War of 1900, in which his actions won the Victoria Cross. At Kut he shared defeat and captivity; his letters record determined efforts to secure help for the men who suffered most.
literature: Lion-Hunting in Somali-land preserves the outlook and practice of a nineteenth-century military sportsman. The diaries and letters of the later campaigns belong to another phase of the same life.
en.legacy: Melliss’s reputation cannot be contained by the hunting narrative. The care he attempted for prisoners after Kut gives his military biography a weight quite different from sporting adventure.
en.bridge: The early book opens one part of a life whose later service and captivity cast a longer historical shadow.
